clue.text: How some feminists have got it to a nicety, I tell you

blocks.clueFragment: How some feminists have got it
blocks.note: some feminists, so the joke goes, have it in for man
done to a nicety is done to a T

explanation.surface: A woman boasting that her feminist friends have perfected some argument, insisting on it to the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'have got it' as 'have got it in for': IN FOR MAN, then T from 'to a T', gives INFORMANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who passes on information is forever saying 'I tell you', so the phrase stands for the person who tells.

clue.text: Chap who helped with the printing in 22 action?

blocks.note: an inker applied ink in the printing process
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A question whether some fellow lent a hand at the press in a Crimean affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is CRIMEAN; an action is a battle. The chap is the man who inks: INKER, then MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was a battle of the Crimean War in November 1854, and an action is a military engagement.

clue.text: Queen in Cornish river's gone native

indicators.note: the royal goes inside the waterway's name

blocks.note: the Fal flows into the sea at Falmouth in Cornwall
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch on a Cornish river has adopted local ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at Britain's south-west tip; ER is the royal cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral animal has escaped domestication and reverted to the wild, which is what going native means.

clue.text: Getting 7 again to care worker with the odd broken cane

indicators.note: read as a thing worked on, so the first word is made to move about
something broken falls apart into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
quaint means odd or curious
taken as written

explanation.surface: A care worker is getting to know someone again, armed with a strange broken walking cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is IN THE KNOW, so getting it again is regaining acquaintance. The parse of 'worker' is loose; 'care' and 'cane' are both rearranged around QUAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacquaintance is becoming familiar again with something, being informed once more about it.

clue.text: Finished andante con moto

indicators.note: con moto is the musical marking 'with movement', so the letters move

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical score marking: a walking-pace movement played with motion, then it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Andante con moto is a genuine tempo marking, so the surface reads as pure music.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at an end is over and done, completed, which is what finished means.

clue.text: Cat - "chat" is translated accordingly

indicators.note: a translated word is rendered differently, so its letters change places

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written; chat is also French for cat

explanation.surface: A French lesson: 'chat' is translated as cat, accordingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on French chat meaning cat, which makes 'translated' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To match means correspondingly, in keeping with something, as accordingly does in 'dress to match'.

clue.text: Feeble specimen of Mayfair politician

blocks.note: Mayfair's London postcode is W1, with the 1 read as the letter I
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sneer at some weak Member of Parliament from the smart London district of Mayfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London whose postcode is W1.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a weak, timid, ineffectual person, which is what a feeble specimen of humanity amounts to.

clue.text: Aware of what's happening with no Ken to help

indicators.note: letters drafted in to help are redeployed and set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone knows what is going on even without a friend called Ken to assist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken also means knowledge, so having no ken looks like the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the know means having inside information, being informed about current events.

clue.text: Capital H for home base?

blocks.note: the French capital
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query whether a capital H is the abbreviation for home or a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital H' looks like an upper-case letter; it is a capital city followed by H.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the local district around a church, one's home patch; 'home base' is a loose, playful fit.

clue.text: I wave - interrupting myself with skill - to show no chance of leaks

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: taken as written
a perm is a hair wave
me is myself
ability is skill

explanation.surface: Someone waving and breaking into their own speech to show nothing will be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: The wave is a hairdo, not a hand gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Impermeability is the property of letting no fluid pass through, so nothing can seep out.

clue.text: Destiny of Eros is about right

indicators.note: the god's name goes round, is about, the following letter

blocks.note: Kama is the Hindu god of love, the Indian counterpart of the Greek Eros
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mythological musing: the fate of Eros, the love god, is basically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros has to be translated into another tradition's love god, Kama, which then wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist thought karma is the force of past deeds that shapes one's fate, hence destiny.

clue.text: 22 stream, a term employed at university

indicators.note: letters that are employed are put to work and deployed in a fresh order

blocks.note: the Alma is a river in Crimea, scene of the first battle of the Crimean War
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spends a term at a university by a river, as if studying in Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is CRIMEAN, so '22 stream' is a Crimean river: the Alma.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for 'nourishing mother', is the usual name for the university or school one attended.

clue.text: Old memento of rare liqueur

indicators.note: the answer is made of part of the following phrase, lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A keepsake bottle of some rare old liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: The old spelling of relic is hidden in raRE LIQUEur.
explanation.definitionFit: A relique, the archaic spelling of relic, is an object kept in memory of the past, a memento.

clue.text: This and this for American hero of mythology

blocks.note: one this and another this make the plural
abbreviation for United States

explanation.surface: A puzzled request for some pronouns to be swapped for a mythological hero in American terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Two of 'this' make 'these', a neat bit of grammar dressed as arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Athenian hero of Greek legend who killed the Minotaur in the labyrinth.

clue.text: Play by members on Indian islands with change of central article

indicators.note: the middle letter of the islands' name is swapped for another word

blocks.note: arms are limbs, members of the body
places what follows after
the Andaman Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal and belong to India
the definite article, replacing the indefinite article A in the middle

explanation.surface: A dramatic production staged by club members on Indian islands, with a grammatical tweak.
explanation.walkthrough: The central A of ANDAMAN is an indefinite article; changing it to THE gives AND THE MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms and the Man is George Bernard Shaw's comedy of 1894, named from the first words of Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Lyme paper provided guide through meadow to park in Nottingham

blocks.note: a map guides
per means through or by way of
a ley is pasture or meadow land

explanation.surface: Directions printed on paper from Lyme lead across a field to a Nottingham park.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria gives two routes: MAP PER LEY, and the letters of 'Lyme paper' rearranged, so 'provided' admits the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Mapperley is a district of Nottingham, with Mapperley Park a well-known residential area there.

clue.text: Actor with quinsy gets silk from dunnock

blocks.note: ... Scales, the English actress of Fawlty Towers
an old name for this throat infection
a strong silk or worsted fabric
the bird's genus name

explanation.surface: An actor with a sore throat receives silk from a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Four senses of one word: an actress, an archaic name for quinsy, a fabric, and the genus of the dunnock, a small British hedge sparrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella Scales is a well-known performer, and the dunnock's scientific name is Prunella modularis.

clue.text: 9 backing for aberrant walrus in standard campaign, 22 or earlier

indicators.note: backing means the number word is written from its end
aberrant means straying from the norm, so the animal's letters wander out of order
the other pieces go inside the word for the norm

blocks.note: the number written out
taken as written
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A strange military scenario of a wayward walrus in a standard campaign, linked with 22 and earlier history.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 9 is the plain number, not a cross-reference to 9-down; the standard is split open to hold the rest. 22 is CRIMEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peninsular War of 1807-14 in Spain and Portugal was a British campaign well before the Crimean War of the 1850s.

clue.text: Shell for kook

blocks.note: first meaning: the case of a nut
second meaning: a crazy person

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the hard case around a nut; colloquially, an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is slang for a mad or eccentric person, and literally the hard outer case of a nut.

clue.text: Release Cleopatra's killer after relative is docked

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts off the end, so the last letter goes
the killer is written following the relative

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
Cleopatra died from the bite of an asp

explanation.surface: A snake that killed Cleopatra is set free once a family member is punished.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp is to undo a fastening and let go, which is to release.

clue.text: Insect found in Russian river, on the bottom

indicators.note: in a down light, on means sitting above, so the river follows

blocks.note: a river bed is its bottom
the Bug is a river of the former Russian Empire, now in Ukraine and Poland

explanation.surface: A creature living in the mud at the bottom of a Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedbug is a small blood-sucking creature that infests beds.

clue.text: Aesthetically pleasing jumbo with gravity for acidity?

indicators.note: one symbol is put in place of another, as for introduces the one taken out

blocks.note: Jumbo was a famous circus elephant, so jumbo means elephant
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
pH is the measure of acidity

explanation.surface: A query whether a large thing turned serious instead of sharp would look attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: In ELEPHANT, the PH of acidity is replaced by G for gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes something graceful and stylish, appealing to the sense of beauty.

clue.text: Russian beginning of Russian novel

indicators.note: only the opening stretch of the book's title is wanted

blocks.note: Only the start of its title is used

explanation.surface: A literary note that something Russian marks the start of a Russian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Crime and Punishment; CRIME AN is where its title begins. Crimea, the theme of this puzzle, was part of the Russian Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimean describes the peninsula of Crimea, which belonged to the Russian Empire at the time of the war.

clue.text: One left in river, not in the country

indicators.note: the pair go inside the waterway's name

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
I for one, L for left

explanation.surface: Someone left behind in a river, away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's homeland; 'not in the country' describes that state, somewhat loosely.

clue.text: 22 hood in lake (cold) and stream (hot)

blocks.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
C for cold, as on a tap
lava is a hot flowing stream of molten rock

explanation.surface: A Crimean hood shown against a backdrop of a cold lake and a hot stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is CRIMEAN: the balaclava helmet was named after the battle of Balaclava, where troops wore knitted hoods.
explanation.definitionFit: A balaclava is a close-fitting knitted hood covering head and neck, named after the Crimean battle.

clue.text: Did Shakespeare say it twice at his marriage?

definitions.text: Did Shakespeare say it twice at his marriage?

blocks.clueFragment: Did Shakespeare say it twice at his marriage?
blocks.note: surface: a historical query about the poet's wedding vows
setter's reading: the bard's first name matches the vow word, so introducing himself and making the vow use the same words

explanation.walkthrough: The groom's vow is 'I will', and Shakespeare, named Will, would say 'I, Will' too: the same words twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the bridegroom's reply in the marriage service, as well as a way of naming the poet himself.

clue.text: Not a Jew, a painter

blocks.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that some artist was not Jewish.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish artist, known for portraits and The Disasters of War.

clue.text: Breathing problem affected my sheep to a degree

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so these words come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Master of Arts, a university degree

explanation.surface: A farmer complains a lung complaint has hit the flock to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease in which damaged air sacs cause shortness of breath.
